title: Bonnie & Blithe
geography: 20 countries; pilot choices United States, Brazil, Poland and China
difficulty_source_label: Overall: Simple; Quant: Low; Analysis: Medium
prompt: Bonnie and Blithe is an international direct selling beauty company. B&B is known for the high quality and value of their beauty products, primarily skincare and makeup. The firm operates in 20 countries and has 1 million sales reps that sell B&B's products directly to consumers. Last year, the company made $1.4 billion in revenue. Due to changing customer preferences, including an increased interest in digital technology and a decreased preference for face-to-face interactions, B&B's sales decreased by 7%. The firm is considering several options to increase profitability moving forward through a digital transformation. How would you evaluate Bonnie and Blithe's options?

clarifying_info.answer: Products are sold exclusively through licensed sales representatives.

interviewer_notes: This is a profitability case disguised as digital transformation. Ask the candidate to keep two solutions and eliminate two using Exhibit 1, then select a pilot geography with Exhibit 2. The book favors social media tools because they support the representative-led model and can be implemented in 6 months. Retain ecommerce for further evaluation, but its 12-month implementation and high delay risk create a first-year-benefit caveat. The recommendation page mistakenly attributes ecommerce's $300 million gross profit to social media. Keep that $300 million as the ecommerce assumption, not a social-media benefit. Exact launch-year cash flow cannot be determined without implementation and ramp timing assumptions.

suggested_framework.summary: Assess digital options through revenue, implementation and operating costs, and risks to the representative-led business model.

children.label: Customers accustomed to representatives may reduce purchases

stages.interviewer_asks: How would you assess the digital transformation options?
stages.release_when: Read the prompt and release clarifications when asked.
stages.info_to_release: B&B operates in 20 countries with 1 million representatives, had $1.4 billion revenue last year and a 7% sales decline. On request: improve profitability in the next year; sales currently occur exclusively through licensed representatives.
stages.expected_answer: Evaluate changes in representative count and productivity, product mix and pricing, then subtract implementation and operating costs. Include implementation timing and risks to customers who prefer representative-led selling. Do not assume a digital project is attractive solely because it grows sales.
good_answer_signals: Clarifies the one-year horizon and existing channel model.

stages.interviewer_asks: Identify two solutions to keep and two to eliminate, explaining your reasoning.
stages.info_to_release: 2017 baseline: 1 million reps, each pictogram representing 100,000; full-time / part-time / for-fun productivity 500 / 100 / 20 units. B&B sells to reps for $10 per unit, costs $9 and earns $1 per unit. Segment revenues are $1.0 / $0.3 / $0.1 billion. Ecommerce: 12 months, high delay risk, $25 million implementation, $150 million annual additional operating cost, $300 million additional annual gross profit with baseline KPIs unchanged, direct-to-consumer sales. Loyalty: 24 months, medium delay risk, $24 million implementation, $10 million annual operating cost, no new reps, additional 50 / 20 / 5 units per rep by tier. Social media: 6 months, low delay risk, $8 million implementation, $4 million annual operating cost, 50,000 new full-time reps, 250 extra units per full-time rep; access only for full-time reps, developed for the top 3 platforms. Phones: immediate, low delay risk, $200 per rep, no listed additional operating cost, 250,000 new reps across all types, no per-rep unit increase.
stages.expected_answer: Keep social media and ecommerce for further evaluation. Social media fits the representative model, has a 6-month implementation and low delay risk. Ecommerce's $300 million annual gross profit is attractive, but 12 months to implement leaves no assured operating period within the next-year objective. Eliminate loyalty because 24 months exceeds the horizon. Eliminate hardware because equipping the existing 1 million reps alone costs $200 million; the source does not specify the mix of 250,000 added reps or whether their phones also incur this cost.
good_answer_signals: Screens timing as well as economic benefits.
Identifies ecommerce's channel and launch-timing risks.
Distinguishes existing-rep hardware cost from unspecified new-rep spending.

stages.interviewer_asks: Quantify the social-media opportunity and compare the retained options on a consistent cost basis.
stages.release_when: Use Exhibit 1 after the option screen; ask the candidate to show calculations.
stages.info_to_release: Use Exhibit 1's $1 profit per incremental unit, 50,000 new full-time reps and 250 extra units per full-time rep. Ecommerce's $300 million annual gross profit is a supplied assumption calculated outside the representative model, not something to derive from rep counts. All listed implementation and annual operating costs still apply.
stages.expected_answer: Baseline full-time reps are $1 billion / ($10 × 500) = 200,000. Social media raises the count to 250,000 and productivity to 750 units. Existing reps add $50 million and new reps $37.5 million, giving $87.5 million annual incremental gross profit, not $300 million. After $4 million annual operating cost, the annual run-rate benefit is $83.5 million; charging the $8 million setup cost against a full operating year gives $75.5 million. Ecommerce gives $150 million annual net operating benefit or $125 million after setup against a full operating year. These are not first-calendar-year forecasts: 6- and 12-month implementations require explicit ramp and cost-timing assumptions. Social media remains the book's preferred feasible near-term pilot, not the largest steady-state benefit.
good_answer_signals: Applies the 250-unit uplift to both existing and new full-time reps.
Subtracts operating and setup costs without mislabeling gross profit as net profit.
Does not transfer ecommerce's $300 million assumption to social media.

stages.interviewer_asks: Which geography should host the pilot?
stages.release_when: After selecting social media, show Exhibit 2.
stages.info_to_release: United States / Brazil / Poland / China: computer literacy 77% / 45% / 72% / 36%; social-media hours per day 1.8 / 3.2 / 1.4 / 1.5; direct-selling beauty market size $4.2 / $5.9 / $0.6 / $5.1 billion; B&B share 4% / 16% / 24% / 1%. The exhibit also shows platform mix and 2015–2017 market-growth trends. Exact unlabeled platform shares and intermediate growth points are not supplied as precise numbers.
stages.expected_answer: Choose Brazil: the highest social-media usage at 3.2 hours/day, largest displayed direct-selling beauty market at $5.9 billion and positive, increasing market growth. Facebook is its leading platform. The US market is shrinking, Poland's market is only $0.6 billion, and China has low B&B share at 1% and relatively low social-media use at 1.5 hours/day. Consider Brazil's lower computer literacy in execution planning.
good_answer_signals: Combines market scale, growth and channel engagement.
Identifies Facebook as the initial Brazilian platform.

stages.expected_answer: Pilot social-media tools in Brazil, starting with Facebook. The program supports the representative model, can be implemented in 6 months and offers $87.5 million annual incremental gross profit before $4 million annual operating cost and $8 million setup cost. Do not promise the source's erroneous $300 million social-media benefit or a full run-rate benefit during the launch year. Brazil combines high usage and the largest growing market among the options. Mitigate implementation delays with a detailed roadmap and buffers; work with marketing to design the program and advertisements.
good_answer_signals: Uses corrected, clearly labeled financial support.
Connects delay risk to timeline buffers and a marketing next step.

math.question: What annual incremental gross profit do social-media tools generate?
givens: $10 per unit; 500 baseline units per full-time rep
50,000 new full-time reps; 250 extra units per full-time rep
math.answer: $87.5 million annual incremental gross profit, matching page 34, not the $300 million attributed to social media on page 37.
math.book_answer_if_different: Page 37 recommends social media because of a one-year timeline and '$300M gross profit'. Page 33 assigns $300 million to ecommerce; social-media arithmetic on page 34 correctly gives $87.5 million.

math.question: What is social media's benefit after project costs?
steps: Annual operating benefit = $87.5 million − $4 million = $83.5 million.
A full operating year's benefit after one-time setup = $83.5 million − $8 million = $75.5 million.
This full-year comparison is not a launch-year forecast; the 6-month implementation and ramp are not modeled by the book.
math.answer: $83.5 million annual net operating benefit, or $75.5 million for a full operating year charged with setup cost. Calendar first-year benefit is unspecified.
math.unit: USD, full operating year after setup cost
math.book_answer_if_different: Page 34 calls $87.5 million the 'total profit increase' without deducting the $4 million annual operating and $8 million one-time costs printed in Exhibit 1. It is the incremental gross contribution, not the all-in project profit.

math.question: What is ecommerce's benefit on the same full-operating-year basis?
givens: Supplied annual incremental gross profit $300 million
steps: Annual operating benefit = $300 million − $150 million = $150 million.
After setup charged to a full operating year = $150 million − $25 million = $125 million.
A 12-month implementation does not establish that this benefit will arrive within the next-year objective.
math.answer: $150 million annual net operating benefit and $125 million after setup on a full-operating-year basis; actual launch-year profit cannot be calculated from the supplied timing information.
math.unit: USD, full operating year after setup cost

math.question: How much does hardware cost for the existing salesforce?
steps: The source does not specify whether the 250,000 added reps also require paid hardware.
math.answer: $200 million for existing reps alone, matching the source's rejection rationale.

synthesis: Pilot social-media tools in Brazil, beginning with Facebook. The 6-month, low-delay-risk program supports the licensed-representative model, and Brazil leads the displayed markets in social-media use and direct-selling beauty market size. Correct annual incremental gross profit is $87.5 million, not the recommendation page's $300 million; annual operating benefit after additional costs is $83.5 million, or $75.5 million for a full operating year charged with setup. These are run-rate economics, not a promised first-year result. Keep ecommerce under evaluation, reject the 24-month loyalty program and costly hardware option, build a roadmap with buffers and engage marketing on program design.
what_great_looks_like: Treats digital transformation as an incremental-profit and timing decision.
Separates new-rep growth from existing-rep productivity improvement.
Identifies the mistaken transfer of ecommerce gross profit to social media.
Chooses Brazil using engagement, market scale and growth, with Facebook as the leading platform.
Flags that annual run-rate economics are not calendar first-year cash flow.
common_pitfalls: Attributing ecommerce's $300 million gross profit to social media.
Ignoring implementation and additional operating costs.
Giving new full-time reps only the incremental 250 units instead of all 750 units.
Assuming a 12-month implementation delivers a full year of benefits within 12 months.
Choosing the US for computer literacy while overlooking its shrinking market.

low_confidence_fields: exhibits[1].data: exact unlabeled platform shares and market-growth points omitted
extraction.notes: Dedup verdict NEW. Read and visually inspected pages 30–37, including a higher-resolution check of Exhibit 1. Both candidate exhibits remain visible: original $300 million ecommerce assumption and unit profit are candidate inputs, not answer leakage. Page 37 incorrectly attributes ecommerce's $300 million gross profit to social media; corrected to $87.5 million annual gross uplift. Page 34 calls that uplift total profit while omitting $4 million annual operating and $8 million setup cost; explicit net comparisons added. Ecommerce's $300 million remains in info_to_release as instructed by the exhibit. The book treats 12-month ecommerce implementation as fitting a next-year objective without accounting for benefit timing; exact launch-year results are not invented. Added full-operating-year comparisons are explicitly labeled and not claimed as launch-year outcomes. Exhibit 2 platform bars and growth lines lack numeric point labels, so only labeled country metrics are tabulated; qualitative trends and original image are retained. The pictogram on page 33 does not clearly distinguish part-time and for-fun reps, so no unsupported count split is stored as an input; the full-time count is independently derivable from labeled revenue and productivity. 'Blythe' in the final prompt sentence is normalized to title spelling 'Blithe'. Overall Simple maps in code to 2; source Low quant difficulty is distinct from our H multi-step quant intensity. Beauty/cosmetics specializes the source Retail / Consumer label. Reviewed and accepted by Claude 2026-10-05.
